name: foraging-spots
note: Lucian's foraging map — source of truth. Each feature: geometry Point [lon,lat]; properties: name, category, species, season, location, notes, added, photos[]. Optional `plant` = a plant slug (filename in src/content/plants/) that links this pin to its field-guide entry both ways; leave it out if no guide exists yet.

properties.name: Saskatoon berry bush
properties.notes: Photographed Jul 4; red pomes with star-crown tip.

properties.name: Crabapple (Verdun/Beatty)
properties.notes: Loaded crabapple at the street crossing, by the bike-path sign.

properties.name: Staghorn sumac
properties.notes: Photographed Jul 27; upright dark-red fuzzy drupe clusters. Steep clusters in cold water for pink 'sumac-ade'; also ground as a tart spice. Don't confuse with poison sumac (white drooping berries, wet ground).

properties.name: Lamb's quarters
properties.season: leaves best late spring–summer, before flowering
properties.notes: Photographed Jul 27; mealy-white new growth, toothed diamond-shaped leaves. Cook like spinach (mild oxalates — eat cooked in quantity). Wild relative of quinoa.

properties.name: Crabapple (Verdun park)
properties.notes: Photographed Jul 29; mature tree loaded with small red pomes, ~2 cm. Tart raw — best cooked into jelly (high pectin), sauce, or fruit leather.

properties.name: Apple trees (bike path)
properties.season: ripe now (windfalls dropping); holds into fall
properties.location: By the bike path (a few young trees lined up)
properties.notes: Photographed Jul 30; a row of young apple trees right beside the bike path. Ripe now — apples on the ground below. Full-size domestic apple; grab off the tree, cook the bruised windfalls.

properties.name: Rowan / Mountain-ash (LaSalle)
properties.season: berries Aug–fall; best after first frost, hold on the tree into winter
properties.notes: Photographed Aug 4; small tree loaded with flat-topped clusters of orange-red pomes, pinnate serrated leaflets. Cook-don't-graze: raw is bitter/irritating, but cooked (ideally after a frost) makes a classic tart rowan jelly. High pectin.
